Notes.Text:
This update for go-containerregistry fixes the following issues:

Changes in go-containerregistry:

- update vendor.tar to address:
  * bsc#1288488, CVE-2026-116591: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd:
    crafted ~27 KB two-block zstd frame makes DecodeAll and the
    streaming decoder panic

  * build(deps): bump the go-deps group across 2 directories with
    4 updates
  * authn: do not overwrite AuthConfig.Auth when username and
    password are empty
  * build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 8
    updates
  * Support pulling images by sha512 digest
  * Allow empty label and annotation values in crane mutate
  * fix(build): Use dependencies.gitSource in cloudbuild_v2.yaml
  * validate: support index attestation manifests and empty
    configs
  * name: improve error when parsing a reference with a URL

  * fix(build): install binaries to /ko-app and add to PATH
  * fix(release): honor declared Go toolchain
  * remote: apply checkRedirectSSRF to writer-side HTTP clients
  * flatten: preserve config and layer media types when
    flattening
  * fix(mutate): make Time layer updates lazy
  * build(deps): bump the go-deps group across 2 directories with
    3 updates
  * remote: copy manifest annotations to referrers fallback tag
    descriptors

Vulnerabilities.Description: An attacker can pass a malicious malformed token which causes unexpected memory to be consumed during parsing.

compress provides various compression algorithms. Prior to 1.20.2, the zstd DecodeAll and streaming decoder paths can panic when a crafted two-block frame reaches huff0.ReadTable with an FSE normalized count of 32768 that readNCount stores in int16 as -32768. The wrapped count allows buildDtable to retain stale fse.Scratch decode-table state from the prior block, and nextFast then derives an out-of-range state and indexes beyond the table instead of returning a decode error. Both blocks are required to preserve and then reuse the stale state, allowing untrusted zstd input to crash an application. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.2.

compress provides various compression algorithms. Prior to version 1.18.7, a signed integer overflow vulnerability in s2.NewDict() allows an attacker to bypass repeat index validation by supplying a dictionary with a uvarint-encoded repeat value exceeding MaxInt64. When Dict.Encode() is subsequently called, the overflowed negative repeat value causes an out-of-bounds memory access via unsafe.Pointer arithmetic, crashing the process with SIGSEGV. This issue has been patched in version 1.18.7.
